metadata.title: Hacktivist & leaktivist catalog: Anonymous, LulzSec, WikiLeaks, LAPSUS$, and the state-aligned DDoS crews
metadata.frame: Batch 3 of the threat-actor catalog: ideologically- or notoriety-motivated actors - classic hacktivist collectives (cDc, Anonymous, LulzSec), leak organizations (WikiLeaks; the Vault 7 CIA dump), notoriety/extortion crews (LAPSUS$ and 'The Com'), and the state-ALIGNED DDoS hacktivism that blossomed around the Russia-Ukraine war (Killnet, NoName057(16), Anonymous Sudan, Ukraine's IT Army). Distinct from state APTs (paid espionage) and ransomware (organized profit) - though the lines blur.
metadata.grade: Group existence, signature operations, and prosecutions = FACT (DOJ indictments; press). The contested links - WikiLeaks as a conduit for GRU-hacked 2016 DNC material; Anonymous Sudan's true sponsor - are ATTRIBUTIONS/INTERPRETATIONS (US IC / vendors) and are graded, with both framings noted. Membership is fluid and often anonymous.
metadata.honest_limits: 'Anonymous' is a banner, not an organization - anyone can act under it, so operations 'by Anonymous' are self-claims. Attribution of leak-org intent (transparency vs foreign-conduit) is contested and presented from both sides. Named individuals behind these groups (informants, defendants) exist in the public record but are referenced in notes, not modeled as nodes.
metadata.method: DOJ indictments (LulzSec/Sabu; Anonymous Sudan 2024; Vault 7/Josh Schulte); US IC assessment on 2016 election interference; vendor + press reporting (LAPSUS$, Killnet, NoName057(16), Guacamaya, IT Army of Ukraine).

edges.notes: The cDc (Cult of the Dead Cow, 1984-) coined the term 'hacktivism', shipped Back Orifice (1998), and spun up Hacktivismo (anti-censorship) - the ideological ancestor of the later leaderless movements (fact).

Anonymous (from ~2008, 4chan roots) = leaderless DDoS + doxxing + defacement hacktivism: Project Chanology (Scientology), Operation Payback (pro-WikiLeaks DDoS on Visa/Mastercard/PayPal 2010), HBGary Federal (2011), Ferguson, #OpISIS. A BANNER anyone can fly, not an org (fact of category).

After the 2022 invasion, actors under the Anonymous banner declared '#OpRussia' - defacements, leaks, and DDoS against Russian state/media targets (self-claimed; attribution to any coherent group impossible by design) (graded).

LulzSec (2011) - a high-profile Anonymous splinter (Sony, PBS, CIA.gov, HBGary) doing it 'for the lulz'; collapsed after leader 'Sabu' (Hector Monsegur) became an FBI informant, leading to arrests of the crew (fact; individuals in public record).
The LulzSec takedown - via a flipped insider informant - is the template for infiltrating leaderless hacktivist crews (fact).

WikiLeaks (2006-, Julian Assange) published massive US government leaks: 'Collateral Murder', the Iraq/Afghan War Logs, and Cablegate (2010) - sourced from Chelsea Manning (convicted 2013, sentence commuted 2017). Landmark transparency/national-security clash (fact; individuals in public record).

March 2017: WikiLeaks published 'Vault 7' - a trove of CIA cyber tools/techniques (Weeping Angel, UMBRAGE, etc.). Ex-CIA engineer Josh Schulte was convicted (2022) as the source - the CIA's analog to the NSA's Shadow Brokers loss (fact).

Vault 7 exposed CIA offensive-cyber capabilities (incl. techniques to mimic other actors' code) - the intelligence-community half of the 'state tools leak' pattern alongside Equation/Shadow Brokers (fact).

CONTESTED: the US IC assessed that GRU/APT28-hacked 2016 DNC/Podesta emails were routed to the public via WikiLeaks (and Guccifer 2.0/DCLeaks). WikiLeaks denied a Russian source. Present BOTH: US-IC attribution of the source vs WikiLeaks' source-protection denial (interpretation/attribution).
LAPSUS$ (2021-22) - teen extortion/notoriety crew (UK/Brazil) from the loose 'The Com' English-speaking cybercrime community; social-engineering + insider-bribery, not ransomware (fact).

LAPSUS$ breached Microsoft, NVIDIA, Okta, Samsung, Ubisoft, and Uber via help-desk vishing, SIM-swaps, and MFA-fatigue - prompting a US Cyber Safety Review Board study of the group's simple-but-effective TTPs (fact).

'The Com' is the broader English-speaking community from which both LAPSUS$ and Scattered Spider emerged - wiring the hacktivist/notoriety layer to the eCrime block (Scattered Spider ran ALPHV ops) (fact).

Killnet (2022-) - pro-Russia DDoS hacktivism against NATO-country government/hospital/airport sites; nationalistic, not state-run but state-aligned (and occasionally suspected of state coordination) (fact/graded).
NoName057(16) - pro-Russia DDoS crew running the crowdsourced 'DDoSia' project (paid volunteers); persistent low-level attacks on European targets; EU/US 'Operation Eastwood' disruption 2025 (fact).

CONTESTED: Anonymous Sudan branded itself as Sudanese hacktivists but researchers linked it to Russia/Killnet; it ran powerful DDoS on Microsoft 365, OpenAI, X, and others (2023). DOJ indicted two Sudanese brothers (2024), complicating the Russia-front theory - present both (graded).

The IT Army of Ukraine (2022-) - a government-ENDORSED volunteer collective coordinating DDoS/defacement against Russian targets. Notable for blurring the civilian/combatant line in cyberwar (a state openly mobilizing volunteer hackers) (fact).
Sustained volunteer DDoS/data-leak operations against Russian banks, media, and services - the mirror image of Killnet/NoName057 (fact).

Guacamaya (2022) - Latin American hacktivists behind mega-leaks of military/police archives (Mexico's SEDENA 'Guacamaya Leaks', plus Chile, Peru, Colombia, El Salvador) - environmental/anti-extractivism motivated; the leaktivism model applied to the Global South (fact).

Killnet/NoName057(16)/Anonymous Sudan mark the STATE-ALIGNED DDoS-hacktivism branch that exploded around the Russia-Ukraine war - deniable nationalist volunteers doing states' low-end disruption (interpretation/category).
LAPSUS$/The Com represent the NOTORIETY-driven, social-engineering-first branch - teenagers defeating big-tech security with vishing/SIM-swaps rather than exploits (fact of category).
